summary: PAPER-DOR-23 is a careful extraction: 59 items, 1 route and 7 source issues, reviewed with formula-level corrections that I confirmed on the page images. All 7 source issues stand. There are 11 findings: 6 medium and 5 low. Medium: (1) a missed source issue. Remark 3.47 allows any h with hKh^{−1} ∩ U = ker θ, but ker θ is non-compact unless F = Q_p. The condition fails at every place of a function field, and fails even for the paper's own diag(1, −π^ν). The review then wrote this condition into items 027 and 050 and into the correction of E7, the recipe for the global counit. The intended condition is the conductor lattice π^{−ν(e)}O. (2) The GL_2 Kirillov model (003) is routed to the new roadmap. R16.2 owns GL_2 Whittaker models ('no second Whittaker model'), and Dospinescu–Le Bras 17 routed the supercuspidal Kirillov model there a day later. The route's own reason still calls the Kirillov model planned. (3) No item states the fact that Theorems 3.42 and 3.52 use without proof: Z_sph → Hom̲(E, E) is an isomorphism, that is, the Bernstein centre of the spherical blocks is the spherical Hecke algebra. Its owner is SmoothRepresentationsPartIIParahoricCenters. (4) Item 053 is marked planned, but its transposition invariance and two-sided action on S(G) (Remark 2.18, Lemma 2.17) come from the central-distribution description of the centre, which SR.3 does not plan. (5) The positive-characteristic Weil representation and function-field theta invariance (059, 006) extend MetaplecticAutomorphicForms in its own direction, from its own primary source, Weil 1964, and belong in a Part II of it. (6) ⊗_G (056) is in Mathlib as Rep.coinvariantsTensor; only its smooth statements are missing, and they belong with SR. Low: the function-field automorphic function spaces now planned in GlobalShtukas GS.0 (036); the implicit Ṽ ≅ V∘(g ↦ g^{−T}) used by Example 3.55; 'Poisson summation on R^n' (Mathlib has ℝ only); Remark 3.54's presentable categories should be imported from EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5; and the report's opening counts are stale. Disclosure: this session wrote PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20 (SmoothRepresentationsPartII) and FIX-RT-AREA-automorphic-1, and red-teamed Treumann–Venkatesh 16. No finding relies on them.

findings.where: PAPER-DOR-23 sourceIssues (a missed issue at Remark 3.47, p. 33); items PAPER-DOR-23/027 and PAPER-DOR-23/050; the correction of PAPER-DOR-23/E7
findings.claim: Remark 3.47 allows any h ∈ GL_2(F) with hKh^{−1} ∩ U = ker(θ). That condition can almost never be met, and the paper's own matrix h = diag(1, −π^{ν(e)}) does not meet it. hKh^{−1} ∩ U is compact, being a closed subgroup of a compact group. But ker θ = {u(x) : e(x) = 1} is compact only when F = Q_p. If F is a finite extension of Q_p of degree at least 2, then e(x) = ψ(Tr(cx)) and ker e contains the Q_p-hyperplane where Tr(cx) = 0. If F = F_q((t)), then e(x) = ψ_0(Tr Res(x c dt)), and ker e contains c^{−1}t^{−n} for every n ≥ 2, because Res(t^{−n} dt) = 0. So in Part II, where every F_v has positive characteristic, the condition fails at every place. For h = diag(1, d) with d = −π^{ν}, h·u(x)·h^{−1} = u(x/d), so hKh^{−1} ∩ U = u(π^{−ν}O). By the definition of ν(e) in Construction 3.44, π^{−ν}O is the largest O-submodule of F on which e is trivial, which is what the remark means. The extraction does not record this. It copies the impossible condition into item 027 ('Any h with hKh^{−1} ∩ U = ker θ may replace diag(1, −π^{ν(e)})'), item 050 ('h_v with h_vK_vh_v^{−1} ∩ U_v = ker θ_v') and the correction of E7 ('a matrix h_v satisfying h_vK_vh_v^{−1} ∩ U_v = ker θ_v'). The review added those corrections. The E7 correction is the instruction the design job will follow to define the global counit, and as written it asks for a matrix that does not exist.

Construction 3.44, p. 31: 'Let ν(e) be the largest integer such that e(π^{−ν(e)}O) = 1'. Construction 3.44, p. 32: the counit uses g = (1 b; 0 1)·diag(1, −π^{ν(e)})·k, and f is 'right-θ-equivariant'. That is well defined exactly because u(π^{−ν}O) = hKh^{−1} ∩ U lies in ker θ. PAPER-DOR-23.result.json: item 027's statement, item 050's statement and sourceIssues E7.correction, quoted above.

findings.claim: The Kirillov model of a generic irreducible representation of GL_2(F), with the Whittaker space and the Whittaker model built from it, is routed to the new exotic-monoidal roadmap as something 'built here'. It is basic local GL_2 theory, and the atlas already names its owner. GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R16.2 owns GL_2 Whittaker models and says there is to be no second Whittaker carrier. AL.3 compares the complex specialisation with 'the classical Whittaker model'. One day after this review, PAPER-DOSPINESCU-LEBRAS-17 (accepted 24 September) routed 'Kirillov model of a supercuspidal representation' to R16.2 by a source route. So the atlas now has two owners of the GL_2 Kirillov model, and the exotic roadmap would build the general case in a roadmap about a monoidal structure. The route also contradicts itself: its 'reason' says 'Kirillov and Whittaker models in SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.5 and GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R16.2/R16.5' are planned, while its 'brief' says 'no stage plans the Kirillov model … so they are built here'.

findings.claim: Theorem 3.42 and the proof of Theorem 3.52 rest on three facts about the spherical generator E = cInd_K^G S(O^×) ≅ cInd_{SL_2(O)}^G 1. E is projective. Its restriction to each Bernstein component is compact. And the action map Z_sph → Hom̲(E, E) is an isomorphism, so End(E) is 'covered by the centre'. The paper calls these 'clear', and no item states them. The third is a real theorem. E ≅ ⊕_η cInd_K^G(η∘det), summed over characters η of O^×. End_G(cInd_K^G 1) is the spherical Hecke algebra H(G//K). The claim is that the Bernstein centre of the unramified block maps isomorphically onto H(G//K), and likewise after twisting by η. The Satake isomorphism does not give this by itself: it needs Bernstein's description of the centre of the Iwahori block and the map from the Iwahori centre to H(G//K). Hom-spaces between different η vanish because the η lie in different blocks. Nothing in the atlas plans this: SR.4 plans Satake for hyperspecial K, and SR.3 plans the centre as End(id). SmoothRepresentationsPartIIParahoricCenters, proposed by PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-18, owns 'the isomorphisms from its center to a parahoric center and spherical Hecke algebra (Haines2009 Theorem3.1.1)'. PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-21/20 routes the GL_2 Iwahori case to R16.2.

findings.fix: Add an item PAPER-DOR-23/060 (theorem). Let F be non-archimedean, K = GL_2(O) and E = cInd_K^G S(O^×) ≅ ⊕_η cInd_K^G(η∘det), summed over the smooth characters η of O^×. Then: (a) E is projective in Mod(G), and its component in each Bernstein component is finitely generated; (b) End_G(cInd_K^G(η∘det)) is commutative and isomorphic to the spherical Hecke algebra H(G//K) twisted by η; (c) the Bernstein centre of the component containing (η̃∘det), for any extension η̃ of η, maps isomorphically onto it; (d) Hom_G(cInd_K(η∘det), cInd_K(η′∘det)) = 0 for η ≠ η′. Hence Z_sph → Hom̲(E, E) is an isomorphism. Locator: p. 31 (after Remark 3.43); proofs of Claim 3.49 (p. 34) and Theorem 3.52 (p. 37). Status: missing. Route it as a part-ii that coalesces with SmoothRepresentationsPartIIParahoricCenters (keep its id, title, parent, area and brief), which owns the centre-to-spherical-Hecke isomorphism, with R16.2 for the GL_2 specialisation. Add the item to route 1's imports.

findings.claim: Item 053 is marked planned, but two of its clauses are planned nowhere: 'Each Z_c is fixed by g ↦ g^T (Remark 2.18)' and '[Z_c] acts identically from both sides of S(G)'. The paper gets both from the description of the Bernstein centre as conjugation-invariant, essentially compact distributions acting by convolution. SR.3 plans the centre only as 'natural endomorphisms of the identity', with 'invariance under inner isomorphisms'. Transposition is an anti-automorphism, and g ↦ g^{−T} is an outer automorphism, so neither is inner. No SR stage plans the distribution description. The only node that plans it is GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.7/bernstein-center-and-local-parameters, for local fields of equal characteristic only, in a packet whose review is still pending. Lemma 2.17 (all three centre actions on Y agree), and through it the isotypic step of Theorem 2.2, depends on both clauses. So does the choice (3.2) of I_RL in Definition 3.2.
findings.evidence: Dor, Lemma 2.17 proof, pp. 14–15: 'because the Bernstein center of G acts on S(G) the same way from both sides … By symmetry (i.e., by conjugation by a permutation from S_3), this also applies to the middle action'. Remark 2.18, p. 15: 'Note that the Bernstein center is fixed by taking the transpose g ↦ g^T. This follows due to the description of the Bernstein center as invariant distributions as any matrix is conjugate to its transpose.' §3.2, p. 19: 'we would like to unambiguously talk about the action of the center of G on a module in a way which is independent of whether we think of it as a left or a right module. This forces us to use equation (3.2)'. content/campaign/SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups/README.md, SR.3: 'Construct the Bernstein decomposition and Bernstein center as natural endomorphisms of the identity, with its action on every object. Prove invariance under inner isomorphisms and compatibility with products.' research/blueprint/packets/GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands.json node GS.7/bernstein-center-and-local-parameters: 'Let G be a reductive group over a local field K of equal characteristic. The Bernstein centre … is, equivalently, … the algebra of central distributions on G(K) acting as multipliers'. research/blueprint/queue.json: REV-GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands pending.

findings.where: PAPER-DOR-23/059 and /006 (route 1, new roadmap); route 1 brief ('the function-field versions are built here from Weil's construction')
findings.claim: The Weil representation over non-archimedean local fields of odd positive characteristic (item 059), and the invariance of the adelic theta functional under rational metaplectic points over a global function field (the metaplectic half of item 006), go to the exotic GL(2) roadmap. Both extend MetaplecticAutomorphicForms in that roadmap's own direction. Its document names this extension: 'Positive-characteristic … covers require a separately sourced extension'. Its primary source, Weil's 1964 Acta paper, is the same construction the review cites for item 059. PROTOCOL §15 says that when a roadmap 'needs more than an existing roadmap covers in the same direction … the additions form a roadmap that extends the existing one, titled "<existing roadmap>, Part II: …"'. It also says a missing general notion is planned 'in the roadmap that owns it: usually the most foundational one'. Routed this way, the exotic-monoidal roadmap would become the atlas's only owner of the function-field Weil representation and theta invariance, which are general tools for any function-field theta correspondence. The route's reason ('a Part II there would mix directions') is about the paper's categorical outputs, not about these two inputs. Only item 009 (the triality lift) is specific to Dor.

findings.claim: Item 056 records the relative tensor product M ⊗_G N as missing: 'The atlas plans only N-coinvariants (SR.2), not the relative tensor product of a right and a left module.' The pinned Mathlib has that construction. Rep.coinvariantsTensor is the bifunctor (A, B) ↦ (A ⊗_k B)_G on Rep k G, for any group G, and its docstring identifies it with A ⊗_{k[G]} B, the right module structure on A being g·a = ρ(g^{−1})a. This is exactly the item's definition: 'the quotient of M ⊗_C N by the span of mg ⊗ n − m ⊗ gn'. The coinvariants functor is a left adjoint (Rep.coinvariantsAdjunction), which gives the item's claim that ⊗_G preserves colimits. The abstract-group analogue of S(G) ⊗_G N ≅ N is also there (Representation.coinvariantsTprodLeftRegularLEquiv: (V ⊗ k[G])_G ≅ V). Genuinely missing are the smooth parts: S(G) ⊗_G N ≅ N for smooth N and a Haar measure, closure of the smooth category, the bi- and tri-module versions and the smooth Tor^G of the proof of Lemma 2.20. Being a basic operation on smooth modules, M ⊗_G N belongs with SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups, which owns coinvariants (SR.2) and the derived smooth category (SR.0:derived-extension). MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.3 also defines big theta modules 'by the appropriate coinvariants', a relative tensor product of the same shape.

findings.claim: The paper silently identifies the contragredient Ṽ, a right module through g^{−1}, with I_RL(V), which is V made a right module through g^T. The Section 2 statement (Theorem 2.2, in terms of Ṽ ⊗_G Y ⊗_G V) and the Section 3 one (Example 3.55, in terms of V ⊛ V = (I_RL V ⊗ I_RL V) ⊗_{G×G} Y) are equivalent only under this identification. It says Ṽ ≅ V∘ι as left G-modules, with ι(g) = g^{−T}. For GL_2 this holds for every irreducible V, since w g w^{−1} = det(g)·g^{−T} gives V∘ι ≅ V ⊗ ω_V^{−1}∘det ≅ Ṽ. For GL_n it is the Gelfand–Kazhdan theorem. No item states it. The extraction's item 033 records 'Theorem 2.2 is equivalent to this being an isomorphism', but not the input that makes it so. Section 4 uses the same identification without comment: 'we will allow ourselves to more implicitly switch between right and left GL_2(A) actions … via the transposition map'.
findings.evidence: Dor, §2.1, p. 7: 'where Ṽ is the contragradient of V, considered as a right G-module'. §3.2, p. 19, (3.1)–(3.2): 'The composition of these two functors is the outer automorphism g ↦ g^{−T} of G'. Example 3.55, p. 35: 'Theorem 2.2 can be simply stated as saying that, for a generic irreducible representation V, the above is an isomorphism.' §4.2, p. 40 (the sentence quoted above). PAPER-DOR-23/033 statement: 'Theorem 2.2 is equivalent to this being an isomorphism for generic irreducible V'. Check: for g = (a b; c d), w g w^{−1} = (d −c; −b a) = det(g)·g^{−T}.

For every irreducible smooth V of GL_2(F), Ṽ ≅ V∘ι with ι(g) = g^{−T}, and so I_RL(V) ≅ Ṽ as right G-modules (with Ṽ acted on through g^{−1}). Proof: w g w^{−1} = det(g) g^{−T} and Ṽ ≅ V ⊗ ω_V^{−1}∘det. Locator: §2.1, p. 7; Definition 3.2, p. 19; Example 3.55, p. 35. Cite it in item 033's statement as the input of the equivalence.
